name: Turkey Migas Skillet
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Austin breakfast-for-dinner skillet, eggs plus crisped tortilla; no egg-forward Tex-Mex dish in the catalog. Source verified at 4 servings, 261 cal / 10g protein as a meatless migas; our build adds 2.5 lb ground turkey to reach ~510 cal / 36g. Confidence: source contains no turkey, numbers are our build. | HARVEST: Source migas recipe contains no turkey; it is an egg-and-tortilla base.
OVERRIDE +93/7 Ground Turkey: ADD title protein: turkey migas needs the turkey; source migas is egg-only. 12 oz browned for 4
OVERRIDE Diced Tomatoes: '1 medium' is a FRESH tomato (123 g), not a 411 g can (bare-count->can convention misfired)
intro_html: Migas started as a way to use up yesterday's tortillas, which is the origin story of most food worth eating. In Austin it means torn corn tortillas fried crisp, then folded into scrambled eggs with peppers, onion and cheese. Add ground turkey and it becomes dinner instead of a hangover cure. Each serving lands at 563 calories with 38 grams of protein for about $2.93 (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (black pepper, salt): ~$0.88. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $27.17 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.94 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $33.48 across 14 servings, roughly $2.39 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $7.53 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $41.01. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.93 a serving (at everyday cost). Eggs and tortillas are two of the cheapest foods in any grocery store, and this dish is built almost entirely out of them plus a couple pounds of turkey.
shop_smart: Corn tortillas are cheaper than flour and they crisp far better. Buy the larger packs, and stale tortillas actually work better here than fresh ones.
Eggs are the cheapest protein per gram in this recipe. Two dozen covers the batch, and they keep for weeks past the carton date.
Jalapenos cost pennies each loose. Buy a handful, freeze what you do not use whole, and they chop straight from frozen.
Red bell peppers are the priciest vegetable here. Green peppers cost less and work fine if the price gap that week is steep.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the corn tortillas into strips and fry them in the vegetable oil in batches over medium-high until they are crisp and lightly browned, then drain them on paper towels.
Pour off most of the oil, then brown the ground turkey in the same skillet, breaking it into crumbles and seasoning it with salt and black pepper.
Add the diced onion, red bell pepper, and jalapeno and cook 6 minutes until they soften, then stir in the drained diced tomatoes and cook off the excess liquid.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt until the yolks and whites are fully combined, with no streaks left.
Drop the heat to medium-low and pour the eggs into the skillet. Push them slowly across the pan with a spatula rather than stirring fast; you want soft folds, not curds.
When the eggs are about three quarters set, fold in the fried tortilla strips so they soften slightly but keep some crunch.
Kill the heat, scatter the Mexican cheese blend over the top, and cover for two minutes to melt it before portioning.
portion_html: Weigh the skillet, subtract the empty pan weight you noted, and divide by 14. Portion while it is still warm, since eggs firm up fast and get harder to scoop clean. Each serving comes to 563 calories and 38 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from chilipeppermadness.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.

head.keywords: turkey migas, migas recipe, tex mex eggs, breakfast for dinner, ground turkey skillet, budget high protein meal prep
steps: Fry corn tortilla strips in oil until crisp, then drain.
Brown the ground turkey in the same skillet and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the onion, red bell pepper, and jalapeno, then add the drained tomatoes and cook off the liquid.
Pour in the beaten eggs over medium-low heat and push them into soft folds.
Fold in the fried tortilla strips, melt the cheese over the top off the heat, and portion into 14 containers.
